subject: prd/tech-design-brainstorm
statement: While interviewing the authority, the skill shall present every question turn in the authority's register rather than the record's: the question phrased in plain language with every house term or corpus anchor glossed inline (never a bare `F-n`/`DQ-n`/`ALT-n`/document reference), grounded in one concrete example — a real case looked up from the basis, code, or corpus where one exists, marked hypothetical or illustrative otherwise, or replaced by an explicit `no example: <reason>` line when no illustrative case exists; for a structural question (a seam, port, or document-class choice) the example is one concrete flow traced through each candidate shape — and carrying an enumerated option set (on a fired panel, the recorded alternatives) in which every option states its outcome on that same example (outcomes pairwise distinct, the FR-3 recommendation marked among them), or one to two sample answers with their meaning where the question is open-form; the record keeps its own register (NFR-2) untouched.
rationale: an authority who cannot cheaply parse a design question either stalls, delegates ("you decide") more than they mean to, or rubber-stamps the recommendation — eroding the provenance the stage exists to produce; one example traced through every candidate shape converts an architecture question into a comparable-outcomes question, and the same-example trace is exactly what makes panel alternatives judgeable rather than wallpaper (UB-7, G3) (operator ruling 2026-07-30)
fit_criterion: across the fixture corpus, 100% of authority-facing question turns carry the form — plain-language question, example or typed skip, enumerated options each stating its outcome on the turn's example (or sample answers for open-form), recommendation marked; zero turns present a corpus anchor without its inline gloss; zero example-bearing turns where two options share an outcome; on fired-panel fixtures, each presented alternative carries its outcome on the turn's example (EVAL-7)
